designCoherence.reason: One system holds across web, portal, app, 3D and exports: Paper/Indigo/Amber grounds, Fraunces statements, JetBrains Mono figures and the day arc appear in home-desktop, portal-desktop, app-today, scene-desktop and og-image alike. Deductions: the app icon is ink-on-amber while the symbol is cream-on-indigo (app-icon.png vs symbol-512.png), the portal Today screen draws two differently shaped arcs with two suns (portal-desktop.png header and chart), and the Arabic product name is 'هالدورا سِل' on the web but 'Haldora Cell' in the Arabic app (app-devices-ar.png).

brandAlignment.reason: Reads calm, warm and plain-spoken: the hero line, the four-moment story (story-chapter-1..4) and the portal's sentence 'At 13:00 the battery holds 100%...' follow 'say what happens, then the number'. No green-on-black, no gloss, no stock people, no fear copy. Held back from 5 by the 3D scene (scene-desktop.png), which uses none of the horizon/landscape language and looks like a generic configurator, and by the hazard-sign black-on-amber app icon.

visualHierarchy.reason: Strong first screen (home-desktop hero, hero-1024) and a clear portal lead sentence, but: battery level on the portal desktop is only a small mono value inside a sentence and in the 'Right now' card (portal-desktop.png), the sticky story panel leaves the bottom third of each viewport empty (story-chapter-1..4, y 610-900), the phone home page shows eight near-identical landscape panels in a row (home-mobile slices 1-3), and the footer is a 20px symbol with two lines of demo text (home-desktop bottom).

typography.reason: Latin pairing is handled well: Fraunces display with tight tracking, Instrument Sans text, mono figures with small units in the portal sentence. Defects: in the app dial 'In the battery' runs into the ring stroke on both sides and '91%' is in the sans, not mono (app-today.png, app-today-dark.png, app-today-evening.png); Arabic small text renders at 10.4-13.3px in my render against the guidelines' 14px floor; the spec '62 x 102 x 16 cm' breaks with a dangling 'x' on phones in both locales (home-mobile, home-ar-mobile).

originality.reason: The day arc is used for real work, not as decoration: as the chart's sun cursor (portal-desktop), the product's only light (scene-desktop), the app dial (app-today) and the scroll story where the sun travels chapter to chapter. The portal's narrated sentence and the history 'sky per day' tiles are not a dashboard template. Template moments remain: the four icon-chip feature cards (home-desktop slice 3), the Devices accordion and the Settings form cards.

motionQuality.reason: Not assessable from stills; score is provisional. From my own frame captures of web/dist at 1440 (8 frames, 700ms apart) the sun does travel along the arc between chapters and the sky crossfades, which matches 'motion moves like light'. But the time chip changes to '18:30' while the sun is still high on the arc, so label and picture disagree mid-transition. Easing, frame pacing and the app's onboarding swipe could not be judged.

interactionClarity.reason: Good: the portal time scrubber drives readout, cursor and sun together and has a table alternative; RTL keeps time left-to-right. Weak: scrubbing past 'Now' rewrites the headline in present tense as fact (portal-forecast.png 'At 18:30 the battery holds 83%'); the app dial's '-'/'+' buttons are unlabelled 8px glyphs (app-today.png); the app reserve slider is driven by up/down chevrons and shows no filled segment in Arabic (app-settings-ar.png); the portal 'Backup reserve 30% · Change' chip gives 'Change' no link or button styling.

assetQuality.reason: Logo system, icons and the layered-horizon plates (og-image, story, social-square, presentation-title) are clean and consistent. Weak: the 3D Cell is a plain rounded box with heavy black vent strokes and a decal-like arc, sitting over a skewed floor band (scene-desktop, scene-finish-2/3); at 21:00 the Chalk finish turns cardboard-tan (scene-evening). The Android adaptive icon reuses the full-bleed square icon, so the launcher mask would crop the horizon and arc feet (my simulation of mobile/assets/icon.png).

presentationPolish.reason: Many surfaces are clean (portal desktop, app devices, guidelines). Visible craft slips: orphan arc dashes beside hero copy (a dash above 'A battery' in home-desktop and home-desktop-dark; the Arabic right leg touching 'بطارية' in home-ar-desktop/-dark), the arc ending in mid-air at 1024 and breaking up at 834/768, a cropped dark-hill lump at the bottom edge of the dark hero (home-desktop-dark, home-ar-desktop-dark around x380-580), the dial label collision, 'Showing a still image.' as raw text on the 3D fallback (scene-still-*), and a near-empty footer.

professionalReadiness.reason: Strong enough to show as work in progress, not yet as finished launch work. Before a client sees it: fix the app dial and the hero arc fragments, write forecast states as forecasts, raise Arabic small text to the brand's own floor, give Android an adaptive foreground, and lift the 3D product presentation. Demo scaffolding is also visible in client-facing places: 'What we hope people will say', 'Simulate being offline' in app Settings, and 'Demonstration data. Nothing is sent anywhere.' next to Save in the portal.

findings.where: Mobile app Today dial (.cis/reports/qa/mobile/app-today.png, app-today-dark.png, app-today-evening.png)
findings.issue: The label 'In the battery' is wider than the inside of the ring: its first and last letters sit on the iris ring stroke on both sides, in light, dark and evening. '91%' is set in the sans, not the mono that the DNA requires for figures. The sun at the apex also touches the top of the ring at 13:00. This is the app's signature element and the first thing a customer sees each day.
findings.suggestion: Shorten the label ('stored') or move it below the ring. Enlarge the ring's inner diameter or reduce the label size so there is at least 8px of clearance. Set the figure in JetBrains Mono. Leave a gap between the sun's path and the ring.

findings.where: Website hero and exports, day arc against text (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png, home-ar-desktop.png, home-ar-desktop-dark.png, hero-1024.png, hero-834.png, home-tablet.png, brand/applications/png/presentation-title.png, og-image.png)
findings.issue: Where the arc is masked around copy, it leaves orphan fragments. At 1440 a single dash sits just above 'A battery', where it reads like a stray accent mark (about x100,y450, both schemes). In Arabic the right leg touches the first word of the subhead 'بطارية' (about x1362,y490-530). At 1024 both legs stop in mid-sky about 200px above the hills. At 834/768 the amber dashes vanish into the brightest band of sky, leaving gaps of 100px or more. On the presentation title a lone segment floats at x195-210,y600-660. The guidelines' construction (arc standing on the horizon) is not met in these compositions.
findings.suggestion: Compose so the arc clears the copy instead of being cut by it: shrink or reposition the arc per breakpoint so both feet land on the horizon outside the text block, or end it with deliberate terminals at the mask edge and suppress fragments shorter than about three dashes. Raise dash contrast where it crosses the pale band of sky. Re-export og-image and presentation-title.

findings.where: Portal Today, forecast state (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-forecast.png)
findings.issue: When the scrubber is moved past 'Now' to 18:30, the large serif sentence says 'At 18:30 the battery holds 83%, the roof is making 0.2 kW and the home is using 2.3 kW' in the present tense. It also keeps 'Bought from the grid so far today: 3.5 kWh', which is the value at Now. The side card becomes 'At 18:30 ... powering the home'. The only cue that this is a forecast is the small caption under the chart, so a prediction reads as fact in the most prominent text on the page.
findings.suggestion: Switch the sentence to forecast grammar when the cursor is after Now ('By 18:30 the battery should hold about 83%...') and show a visible 'Forecast' tag next to the time. Hide or relabel the 'so far today' clause, and retitle the side card 'Expected at 18:30'.

findings.where: Android launcher icon (mobile/app.json android.adaptiveIcon, mobile/assets/icon.png = brand/applications/png/app-icon.png)
findings.issue: The adaptive icon's foreground is the full-bleed square amber icon, and its horizon bar runs to within about 4% of the edges. Android shows only the central safe zone of an adaptive foreground. In my circular-mask simulation (own render, not a QA screenshot) the horizon bar and both arc feet are cut off. The #14152B background never shows, because the foreground is opaque.
findings.suggestion: Export a transparent adaptive foreground with the arc, sun and horizon inside the central 66% safe zone, and set the background colour or a separate background layer. Check the result in circle, squircle and rounded-square masks.

findings.where: 3D product presentation (.cis/reports/qa/scene/scene-desktop.png, scene-desktop-dark.png, scene-evening.png, scene-finish-2.png, scene-finish-3.png, scene-ar.png, scene-mobile.png, scene-tablet.png)
findings.issue: The brief asks for an interactive 3D presentation of the Cell. The scene is a utility configurator: a rounded box with an inset panel, a printed-looking arc and seven heavy black vent strokes, in front of a flat diagonal floor band whose angle does not match the camera. There is no horizon or landscape, no brand mark and no narrative. At 21:00 the Chalk finish renders as cardboard tan, and the Dusk finish reads as saturated ultramarine rather than the muted Indigo it names. The finish chips wrap 'Ember' onto its own row in a panel that has room to spare (scene-desktop.png).
findings.suggestion: Refine the model (chamfered edges, a panel seam, matte powder-coat roughness, vents as recessed slots rather than black lines). Make the arc an emissive element that dims at night. Replace the floor band with a wall/floor plane lit from the upper left, and bring in the time of day through window light or a horizon. Add the lockup and a one-line caption per time of day. Keep the three finish chips on one row.

findings.where: Arabic small text across web and portal (own render of web/dist/ar/ and app/dist/?lang=ar at 1440 and 390; visible in .cis/reports/qa/web/home-ar-desktop.png, home-ar-mobile.png, app/portal-ar-mobile.png, portal-history-ar-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The guidelines say Arabic is 'never set ... below 14px', and the brief asks for Arabic typography that is 'not an afterthought' and text 'readable at arm's length'. In my render the scroll cue 'مرّر لتتابع اليوم' and the portal phone tab labels (اليوم، الأجهزة، السجل، الإعدادات) are 10.4px, the chart label 'الآن' is 12px, and stat captions, spec labels, form labels, testimonial attributions and the portal 'آخر تحديث' line are 13.3px.
findings.suggestion: Set an Arabic floor of 14-15px for labels and captions (Arabic needs a larger size than Latin at the same nominal size), and 12px+ equivalents only for Latin. Re-check the tab bar and chart labels at 390px.

findings.where: Marketing page on phone: feature cards repeat the story art (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-mobile.png, home-mobile-dark.png, home-ar-mobile.png, home-ar-mobile-dark.png; also home-desktop.png slice 3)
findings.issue: On a phone the four story chapters (sunrise, noon, sunset, night panels) are followed immediately by four feature cards that use the same four landscape panels. That makes eight near-identical sky tiles in one scroll. The 'Clever, and happy to explain itself' section reads as filler, and the signature loses impact through repetition. The amber icon chip on each card adds a third visual layer that says nothing the picture does not.
findings.suggestion: Give the features their own visuals from the product and the data: a crop of the portal chart for 'The day, drawn as a curve', the reserve band for 'A reserve you set once', the app dial for 'It learns the shape of your day'. Alternatively drop the pictures from the cards on phone and keep the icon. Remove either the chip or the picture.

findings.where: Hero sun and header (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, hero-1024.png, hero-834.png, home-mobile.png, home-ar-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The sun's outer halo sits behind the navigation: at 1440 and 1024 it is behind 'A day with Haldora', and on phone and tablet the hamburger icon sits inside the halo. Header and illustration compete at the very top.
findings.suggestion: Drop the sun about 60px lower, or start the hero illustration below the header bar.

findings.where: Hero scroll cue (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, hero-1024.png, home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: 'SCROLL TO FOLLOW THE DAY' is about 10px pale text on the mid-taupe hill. Its contrast is low and it is barely visible. The Arabic cue is 10.4px.
findings.suggestion: Set it at 13px+ in Ink/Parchment on a flat area, or remove it.

findings.where: Dark hero bottom edge (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop-dark.png, home-ar-desktop-dark.png; light: home-desktop.png bottom right)
findings.issue: A cropped dark hill lump sits on the section boundary at about x380-580, y880-900 in the dark hero, and a dark sliver shows at the bottom right of the light hero. Both read as clipping artefacts.
findings.suggestion: Let the front range span the full width at the boundary, or clip the hills above the section edge.

findings.where: Scroll story layout and timing (.cis/reports/qa/web/story-chapter-1.png to story-chapter-4.png; own frame capture of web/dist)
findings.issue: The sticky picture panel sits in the top two thirds of the viewport, with about 290px of empty ground beneath it on every chapter. In my frame capture the time chip switches to the next chapter's time while the sun is still travelling, so for a moment the label and the sun disagree.
findings.suggestion: Centre the panel vertically, or let it fill the viewport height. Tween the time chip with the sun, or update it when the sun arrives.

findings.where: Website footer (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, home-mobile.png, home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: The footer is a 20px symbol and two lines of demonstration text below roughly 150px of blank space. There is no wordmark, navigation, language switch or contact line, so the page ends looking unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Design a footer: lockup, the four section links, language and appearance toggles, and a small horizon band to close the day.

findings.where: Contact section background ('Ask about your roof', .cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png, home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: A tiled pattern of interlocking loops covers the section behind the headline and body copy. It is the busiest texture on the page, is not one of the DNA's motifs (arc, horizon, grain) and lowers the legibility of the lead text.
findings.suggestion: Replace it with paper grain or a low horizon band, or keep the pattern only behind the form card.

findings.where: Testimonials headline (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-desktop.png, home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: 'What we hope people will say' / 'ما نرجو أن يقوله الناس' is honest for a demo, but on a launch page it undercuts the 'trustworthy' perception the brief asks for.
findings.suggestion: For client presentation, use a neutral headline and mark the quotes as placeholders in the presentation notes rather than on the page.

findings.where: Portal Today, two arcs and two suns (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-desktop.png, portal-desktop-dark.png, portal-ar-desktop.png, portal-tablet.png)
findings.issue: The header draws a very flat arc with a sun, and the chart draws a tall arc with a second sun, on the same screen. The guidelines say 'Do not draw two arcs or two suns in one picture', and the header arc does not follow the stated construction (50% of height).
findings.suggestion: On Today, let the chart's sun be the only sun: drop the header sun on this route, or turn the header into a plain time stamp.

findings.where: Portal chart legibility (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-desktop.png, portal-desktop-dark.png, portal-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: kW lines and the battery % line share one plot with no y-axis or scale, so the curve heights cannot be read, only compared. The 'Now' / 'الآن' label collides with the battery dashed line. In dark mode the roof fill turns a muddy brown (around x600,y850).
findings.suggestion: Add a light kW scale on one side and a % scale (or end labels) for the battery line. Offset the Now label. Use a translucent amber or a Rose tint for the dark-mode fill.

findings.where: Portal reserve shortcut (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-desktop.png, portal-mobile.png)
findings.issue: 'Backup reserve 30% · Change' is one pill and 'Change' has no link or button styling. The brief's success measure is changing the reserve in under ten seconds.
findings.suggestion: Make 'Change' a visible text button (underline or Indigo pill) that opens the reserve control in place.

findings.where: Portal History encoding and colour (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-history.png, portal-history-mobile.png, portal-history-ar-mobile.png)
findings.issue: The fortnight tiles differ only by a slightly paler amber dome, so 46% and 100% days look nearly the same at a glance. Every tile shows the sun at noon. The 'Self-powered' bars in the table use a pale mint fill, which is a dark-scheme success colour, not a light-scheme data colour.
findings.suggestion: Encode the share in position (sun height or arc length) as well as tint. Use Amber or Iris for the table bars.

findings.where: App controls (.cis/reports/qa/mobile/app-today.png, app-settings.png, app-settings-ar.png, app-settings-ar-dark.png)
findings.issue: The '-' and '+' under the dial have no label and their glyphs are about 8px. The horizontal reserve slider is stepped with up/down chevrons. In Arabic the slider shows no filled segment at all, so 30% is not visible as a bar.
findings.suggestion: Label the stepper ('See another time') and use the brand plus/minus icons at 20px. Use minus/plus or start/end chevrons for the reserve. Fix the RTL fill.

findings.where: App Settings demo control (.cis/reports/qa/mobile/app-settings.png, app-settings-dark.png, app-settings-ar.png)
findings.issue: 'Simulate being offline' sits in customer-facing Settings, next to Alerts. A client will read it as a product feature.
findings.suggestion: Hide it behind a demo build flag or a developer menu.

findings.where: App night state (.cis/reports/qa/mobile/app-today-evening.png)
findings.issue: At 21:00 the crescent is drawn in dark Indigo on the light card. The guidelines specify a smaller pale crescent at night, and the moon sits at the arc's apex, which says nothing about the time.
findings.suggestion: Use the night card treatment (Night ground, Parchment crescent) after sunset, or a pale crescent placed by time.

findings.where: Arabic naming and units (.cis/reports/qa/mobile/app-devices-ar.png, app-device-detail-ar.png, web/home-ar-desktop.png)
findings.issue: The web's Arabic names the product 'هالدورا سِل', but the Arabic app lists 'Haldora Cell' and 'Haldora Sense' in Latin. The spec block uses kW/kWh/cm/dB while the Arabic body copy writes 'كيلوواط'.
findings.suggestion: Pick one rule for product names in Arabic (the guidelines allow هالدورا in running text) and apply it in the app and on the web. State the unit rule in the guidelines and follow it.

findings.where: Spec line breaks (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-mobile.png, home-ar-mobile.png, product-mobile.png)
findings.issue: '62 × 102 × 16 cm' breaks after '102 ×' on phones. In Arabic the dangling '×' ends up at the start of the run.
findings.suggestion: Join the dimensions with non-breaking spaces, or set them smaller on phone.

findings.where: 3D still fallback (.cis/reports/qa/scene/scene-still-desktop.png, scene-still-mobile.png, scene-still-tablet.png, scene-still-dark.png)
findings.issue: The fallback shows 'Showing a still image.' as raw grey text in the top-left corner. It reads like a debug message, and the time control disappears without explanation.
findings.suggestion: Write it as a caption in the panel ('A still view. Turn on motion to explore.') and keep the finish chips working on the still.

findings.where: App icon colourway (brand/applications/png/app-icon.png, brand/logo/png/symbol-512.png)
findings.issue: The app icon is an ink arc on an amber field. Elsewhere the symbol is cream on Indigo, or Indigo on amber in dark contexts. Black on amber also reads as hazard signage, which is the opposite of 'calm, warm'.
findings.suggestion: Use the Indigo tile with a cream arc and an amber sun, as on the logo symbol and touch icon, or document the amber variant as a deliberate night/dark rule.

findings.where: Brand guidelines, day arc section (brand/guidelines.html)
findings.issue: The construction diagram draws three suns (dawn, noon, dusk) in one picture, directly above the rule 'Do not draw two arcs or two suns in one picture'. The 'Do not outline' misuse tile shows an empty rounded square, not an outlined mark.
findings.suggestion: Ghost the dawn and dusk positions as hollow markers and label the diagram as a construction drawing. Show the actual outlined symbol in the misuse tile.

findings.where: Localised social pairs (brand/applications/png/social-square.png vs social-square-ar.png; story.png vs story-ar.png)
findings.issue: The English square is 'Evening runs on noon' and the Arabic square is the sunrise chapter. The stories likewise pair sunrise with noon, so the set cannot run as one bilingual post.
findings.suggestion: If the pairs are meant for a bilingual campaign, export each scene in both languages.

findings.where: Portal phone branding (.cis/reports/qa/app/portal-mobile.png, portal-ar-mobile.png)
findings.issue: On phone widths the portal shows no Haldora mark anywhere. The sidebar lockup disappears and the bottom tab bar has none.
findings.suggestion: Put the symbol at the start of the date row.

findings.where: Arabic: designed or mirrored (.cis/reports/qa/web/home-ar-*.png, app/portal-ar-*.png, mobile/*-ar*.png, brand og-image-ar/story-ar/social-square-ar)
findings.issue: The Arabic reads as designed copy on a mirrored layout. The copy is idiomatic, not literal ('المساء يعمل بطاقة الظهيرة'). The arc, charts and time sliders correctly keep sunrise-to-sunset left to right. Navigation, the sidebar, tab bars, chevrons and pagination mirror correctly. Headings use IBM Plex Sans Arabic 700 with generous leading. The page compositions themselves are the English ones mirrored, and the Arabic loses the serif/sans contrast that gives the English its editorial voice. The guidelines accept this, but it makes the Arabic quotes and statements feel plainer.
findings.suggestion: Consider one Arabic-specific composition move (for example, statements set larger with more air, or quotes with an amber rule) so the Arabic has its own editorial voice.

findings.where: Prohibited patterns check (all deliverables)
findings.issue: None of the DNA's prohibited patterns appear: no green-on-black dashboards, no glossy renders on white, no neon glows or lens flares, no stock photography, no lightning-bolt imagery in use, no outage fear copy. The 'quiet reserve' copy talks about the street going dark as reassurance, not as a threat.

findings.where: Strengths to protect
findings.issue: The hero line and first screen, the four-moment story with the sun travelling the arc, the portal's narrated sentence with mono figures, the chart's sun-above-the-cursor, the history 'sky per day' idea, and the warm night palette are distinctive and specific to this client. They should survive revision.

findings.where: earlier review: Cell configurator at phone width
findings.issue: Fixed. At 390px the viewer now stacks: the canvas is full card width (about 325x350) above the Finish and Time controls in home-mobile.png, home-mobile-dark.png, home-ar-mobile.png and product-mobile.png, and the Cell and its arc are fully visible.

findings.where: earlier review: Portal History fortnight tiles
findings.issue: Partly fixed. The caption now matches the drawing ('The warmer the sky, the more of that day the home ran on its own power. The figure under each day gives the share.'). But every tile is still the same filled dome with the sun at the apex, and the value is still carried mainly by a subtle tint difference (Fri Nov 6, 46%, versus Sun Nov 1, 100%, in portal-history.png and portal-history-mobile.png).

findings.where: earlier review: Website hero arc against the copy block
findings.issue: Partly fixed. The arc now appears masked around the text block. But a lone dash still sits just above 'A battery' at 1440 (home-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png). The Arabic right leg still touches 'بطارية' (home-ar-desktop.png, home-ar-desktop-dark.png around x1362,y490-530). At 1024 the legs still stop in mid-sky (hero-1024.png), and at 834/768 the arc still breaks up in the pale sky (hero-834.png, home-tablet.png).

findings.where: earlier review: Light-scheme horizon hills
findings.issue: Partly fixed. The far and middle ranges are now warm (sampled #E1D8C4 and #B2A998 in story-chapter-2.png and hero-834.png), and the first screen no longer reads cold. The front range is still a neutral grey-violet that is not in the palette (#4E4C56 on the web, #4B4B54 in og-image.png), and the middle taupe is also off-palette.

findings.where: earlier review: App icon masters
findings.issue: Partly fixed. The 1024 icon is now a full-bleed amber square (app-icon.png) and the 180 touch icon is full-bleed Indigo (apple-touch-icon-180.png), so the tile-inside-a-tile problem is gone. No separate Android adaptive foreground was produced: mobile/app.json reuses the same full-bleed icon as the adaptive foreground, which crops the artwork (see the new major finding).

findings.where: earlier review: Mobile app Today dial
findings.issue: Partly fixed. The ring now sits fully above the horizon line (app-today.png), so the two metaphors no longer collide at the ground. '91%' is still set in the sans, not mono. The '-'/'+' stepper is still unlabelled with roughly 8px glyphs. A new collision has appeared: 'In the battery' overlaps the ring stroke.

findings.where: earlier review: Feature cards look like a stock grid
findings.issue: Fixed as described. All four cards now carry day-arc landscape illustrations (noon, night, sunrise, sunset), card 4 has one, and the dark scheme uses the same night-friendly scenes on dark cards (home-desktop.png, home-desktop-dark.png, home-tablet.png, home-ar-desktop.png). The new problem is repetition of the story art (see the new major finding), and the amber icon chips keep a template feel.
